items.title: Commission to investigate how Booking.com combats scams and fraud under the Digital Services Act
items.description: Commission to investigate how Booking.com combats scams and fraud under the Digital Services Act Anonymous (not verified) Wed, 10/21/2026 - 12:06 Today, the European Commission has opened formal proceedings to assess whether Booking.com may have breached the Digital Services Act (DSA) by not having diligently assessed or effectively mitigated risks related to fraudulent listings and phishing scams. The platform may also have breached the DSA when it comes to transparency because it did not clearly label as ads those listings whose providers paid for a higher ranking in search results shown to users. The investigation will focus on the following areas: Fraudulent and non-compliant listings on Booking.com Phishing scams exploiting Booking.com's reservation and guest data Paid-for boosted listings not clearly identifiable as advertisements Read the full details in the press release Find fur

items.title: Digital Services Act study on financial scams on online platforms and ways to counter them
items.description: Digital Services Act study on financial scams on online platforms and ways to counter them Anonymous (not verified) Tue, 10/20/2026 - 08:47 A new study maps the main types of online financial scams, platform features scammers exploit, their impact on users and society and measures platforms can take to stop them. Online financial scams – fraudulent schemes whose primary aim is to extract money from victims – have grown into a pervasive crime in the digital age. They are present across all types of online intermediary services, including Very Large Online Platforms (VLOPs) and Very Large Search Engines (VLOSEs) . The European Commission has procured this study in 2025 to support its supervisory and enforcement tasks under the Digital Services Act (DSA) . items.title: First harmonised standard supporting the AI Act published in the Official Journal
items.description: First harmonised standard supporting the AI Act published in the Official Journal Anonymous (not verified) Mon, 10/19/2026 - 09:37 The European Commission has published the reference to the first harmonised standard supporting the implementation of the AI Act in the Official Journal of the European Union. The standard, EN 18286:2026 - Artificial intelligence - Quality management system for EU AI Act regulatory purposes , developed by CEN and CENELEC, provides a clear legal pathway for providers of high-risk AI systems to comply with the quality management system requirements under article 17 of the AI Act . Its publication through Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/2274 means that providers implementing this standard will benefit from a presumption of conformity with the Article 17 requirements covered by the standard.
